item_name: Confidence and refusal: when confidence stops separating right and wrong answers and how to check this in our project
bibliography: (1) Paul F. Jaeger, Carsten T. Lueth, Lukas Klein, Till J. Bungert. A Call to Reflect on Evaluation Practices for Failure Detection in Image Classification. ICLR 2023 (oral). arXiv:2211.15259 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.15259); code: FD-Shifts benchmark, https://github.com/IML-DKFZ/fd-shifts [uncertain - repository not opened]. (2) Leo Feng, Mohamed Osama Ahmed, Hossein Hajimirsadeghi, Amir Abdi. Towards Better Selective Classification. arXiv:2206.09034 v4 (1 Mar 2023); arXiv page lists no venue, outline states ICLR 2023 [uncertain]. (3) Alejandro Monroy Munoz, Rajeev Verma, Alexander Timans. Detecting Object Tracking Failure via Sequential Hypothesis Testing. arXiv:2602.12983 v1 (13 Feb 2026), WACV workshop 'Real World Surveillance: Applications and Challenges, 6th'; no code link found. (4) Carl Doersch et al. TAPIR: Tracking Any Point with per-frame Initialization and temporal Refinement. ICCV 2023, arXiv:2306.08637 (not re-read in this pass). (5) Nikita Karaev et al. CoTracker3: Simpler and Better Point Tracking by Pseudo-Labelling Real Videos. arXiv:2410.11831 (HTML v1 read for tables). (6) Tianyang Xu, Zhen-Hua Feng, Xiao-Jun Wu, Josef Kittler. AFAT: Adaptive Failure-Aware Tracker for Robust Visual Object Tracking. arXiv:2005.13708 (preprint, no venue listed). (7) Alan Lukezic, Luka Cehovin Zajc, Tomas Vojir, Jiri Matas, Matej Kristan. FuCoLoT - A Fully-Correlational Long-Term Tracker. arXiv:1711.09594; ACCV 2018 [uncertain - arXiv page lists no venue].
full_text_checked: Short screening. Read: arXiv abstracts of (1), (2), (6), (7); full HTML of (3) (method, Tables 1-3, figures, limitations); CoTracker3 HTML (Table 1, Tables 5, 7, 8 and confidence/visibility head description). Not read: full texts of Jaeger et al. and Feng et al. (metric recommendations taken from abstract plus prior knowledge, marked uncertain), TAPIR full text, AFAT and FuCoLoT full texts.
task_and_output: (1)/(2): image classification with a confidence score used to reject (abstain) - output: class + scalar confidence; evaluation by risk-coverage. (3): online SOT failure alarm - output: a binary alert when an e-process over per-frame quality crosses 1/alpha. (4)/(5): point tracking with per-point position plus separate occlusion (visibility) and accuracy-confidence outputs. (6): Siamese SOT plus a predicted per-frame tracking-quality score. (7): long-term correlation-filter tracker with target-loss detection and image-wide re-detection. For us: a per-episode decision 'apply the FlyVis correction / refuse' ranked by a confidence score.
data_and_independent_videos: (1): image classification datasets with in-distribution, covariate-shift and new-class test splits (details not read). (3): OTB-100, LaSOT, TrackingNet, GOT-10k - 50 randomly sampled videos per dataset, each repeated in 50 noisy trials; trackers KCF and SiamFC. (5): TAP-Vid DAVIS, Kinetics, RoboTAP; trained on Kubric synthetic + 15k real videos with pseudo-labels. Others not read in detail.
target_size_and_input_resolution: not applicable (screening; no transfer of resolution-dependent mechanism).
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: not applicable for (1)/(2); (3) native benchmark frame rates, failure defined after 2 s (supervised) or 10 frames (unsupervised) below tolerance; others not reported in this screening.
detector_and_exemplar: not applicable (screening). (3): trackers initialised from the first-frame box; no detector.
trainable_nodes_and_loss: (1): no new model - benchmark of existing confidence scoring functions. (2): classifier trained with selective-classification methods plus an entropy-minimisation regulariser; selection by the classifier's own scores. (3): no training; betting rate lambda learned online (aGRAPA or SF-OGD). (5): CoTracker3 confidence head trained with BCE to predict 'track within 12 px of ground truth', visibility head with BCE on visibility; on pseudo-labelled data these heads are frozen. (6): ConvLSTM Quality Prediction Network over response-map history. (7): hand-designed.
controls_seeds_splits: (1): large-scale comparison of confidence functions across failure sources (the key control is the plain softmax-response baseline, which wins overall). (2): compares architectural selection heads against selection by the classifier's own scores on the same trained models. (3): 50 noisy trials per video for empirical false-alarm rate; no head-to-head against raw peak/entropy thresholds. (5): Table 7 frozen vs trained visibility head ablation. No seeds/CIs extracted in this screening.
metrics_and_numbers: (1): headline finding (abstract) - simple softmax response is the overall best confidence scoring function across failure sources; recommended single metric AURC (area under risk-coverage curve), because AUROC of failure detection ignores the classifier's accuracy [uncertain - from prior knowledge, full text not read]. (2): gains of selection heads (SelectiveNet, Deep Gamblers, SAT) attributed to a better-trained classifier, not to the head; selecting by the classifier's own scores performs better across coverages (abstract). (3) Table 3 (supervised NGIoU, alpha 0.1): false-positive rate <= 10 % everywhere, e.g. SiamFC aGRAPA OTB-100 FPR 6.12 %, average detection delay 44.93 frames; LaSOT 0.60 % / 177.62 frames; KCF SF-OGD LaSOT 6.64 % / 102.13 frames; Fig. 5: peak correlation stays high despite drift (missed alert). (5) CoTracker3 Table 1: online, Kubric + 15k, DAVIS occlusion accuracy OA 90.2 (AJ 63.8, delta_avg 76.3); offline Kub+15k DAVIS OA 91.2. Verification of the outline's unverified claim: '90.2 %' is correct (OA, DAVIS, online, Kub+15k, Table 1), but '77.9 %' is NOT a paired number - it is delta_avg on RoboTAP for the 'Averaging' teacher-selection ablation in Table 8 (Appendix C); the secondary source combined two unrelated numbers.
tested_conditions: (1): distribution shift - yes (covariate shift and new classes); similar distractors / tracking - no. (3): unseen videos - yes; target absence - not reported; similar distractors - no (authors list target switching and camouflage as future work); occlusion - not reported (future work); night/low light - not reported; sequential operation on own predictions - yes (online). (5): occlusion - yes (visibility head); others not reported in screening. (2), (6), (7): not reported in this screening.
mechanism_summary: Published findings: (a) a confidence score can rank errors well inside one distribution yet lose separation under covariate shift or on new failure sources; only an evaluation covering all failure sources with a risk-aware metric (risk-coverage, AURC) shows this, and a plain confidence from the predictor itself often beats dedicated heads (Jaeger; Feng). (b) Per-frame map-quality scores (peak, sharpness) can stay high while the tracker follows the wrong object, so single-frame thresholds give missed alarms; accumulating per-frame evidence in a sequential test (e-process) controls the false-alarm rate at a chosen level at the cost of detection delay (Monroy Munoz et al.). (c) Point trackers separate two questions with two outputs - 'is the point visible' and 'is my position within N px' (TAPIR, CoTracker3). (d) Tracking-quality history as input to failure prediction (AFAT ConvLSTM; FuCoLoT compares current response quality with its history). Proposed for us (not published): use (a) and (b) as a measurement protocol before any new refusal module.
transfer_limits: (1)/(2) are image classification with thousands of test samples; our selection operates on 1786 positive train26 rows and ~84 selected at 1 % coverage, so AURC differences will have wide CIs and must be bootstrapped by video. (3) reports detection delays of 25-178 frames on long videos; our loss episodes last at most 30 frames at 30 Hz, so a sequential test with similar delays would alarm after the episode ends; tolerances were hand-set by inspection. (5) requires dense ground truth for 'within N px' and visibility; our labels are 5 Hz annotations of visible objects only (unknown rows: 20 of 84 selected at 1 % in z13_target_center_v1). Distractor case (right object vs similar neighbour) is not tested by any screened source except as stated future work.
research_questions_addressed: 5.1 (right object and refusal): design caution and a direct evaluation recipe - map maximum or peak quality does not imply the right object (Monroy Munoz Fig. 5); refusal must be judged by risk-coverage/AURC including the transfer train26 -> dev35. 5.2: indirect (memory write gates in other items rely on such confidences). 5.3: caution from Feng et al. - a gain attributed to a refusal head may come from a better underlying predictor; separate the two. 5.4: refusal is applied before matching; its value must be measured by matching outcomes, not only by ranking.
candidate_node_change: No node change as the primary output; a measurement protocol first (it decides whether any confidence-based refusal is worth building): (1) For every existing readout score (centered D, C, R1, absolute height, map-utility heads) compute the risk-coverage curve and AURC of 'useful vs harmful correction' on train26 and, frozen, on dev35, with the oracle AURC and a random-ranking reference; paired bootstrap by video. (2) If all scores are near random on dev35 (AURC excess over oracle not separable from random), confidence-based refusal on FlyVis maps is not viable and the next change must target localisation or association, not refusal. (3) Only if some score separates within episodes but not per frame: test a sequential accumulation over the search frames of the loss episode (e-process-style, alarm/refusal rate fixed in advance) as a readout-state change of FlyVis (evidence carried in a recurrent readout state). Controls: same protocol on R1 input-eye features (no fly), on stock C, and on a Kalman-innovation score without any fly signal. Stop condition: if the FlyVis-based score's AURC is not better than the R1 or Kalman-innovation score (paired CI including zero), refusal is not a FlyVis result.
strongest_objection: The screened sources are evaluation and classification studies, plus one 2026 workshop paper with two weak trackers (KCF, SiamFC), hand-set tolerances and no distractor tests; none shows a refusal mechanism that separates the right object from a similar neighbour. They justify a measurement, not an implementation, and our small number of selected rows (84 at 1 % coverage) may make AURC comparisons inconclusive.
evidence_strength: (1) peer-reviewed ICLR 2023 oral with public benchmark code (moderate-strong for classification); (2) preprint/possibly ICLR 2023 (moderate); (3) workshop paper, 2 trackers, no code (weak); (5) preprint with public code, numbers verified in tables (moderate); (6)/(7) older preprint/conference works not read in full (weak in this screening). Overall: moderate as methodology, weak as evidence for a tracking refusal mechanism.
where_distinction_is_made: (1)/(2): in a separate decision (thresholding a confidence score), with evidence that the score should come from the predictor itself. (3): in a separate sequential decision over accumulated per-frame quality; the unsupervised quality cannot distinguish 'tracking a different object well' from correct tracking (stated limitation). (4)/(5): in the representation/heads - separate outputs for presence (visibility) and position accuracy, so a confident peak with an occluded point can be refused. Map maximum vs right object: explicitly NOT separated by peak-based quality in (3) (Fig. 5).
feature_dependence: Methodological sources are feature-agnostic (any score). The sequential test only needs a scalar per-frame quality - applicable to FlyVis map statistics; but its unsupervised signals (peak correlation, sharpness) are exactly those that fail on distractors. CoTracker3/TAPIR heads rely on large RGB feature trackers.
association_consequence: Refusal changes whether the FlyVis correction is applied before matching; the effect on HOTA comes only through corrected vs uncorrected Kalman centers (z13_center_hota_v1: 61.6584 vs 61.6548). An external guard rule (shift limit, match-cost check as in the R1 case 0.123 -> 1.0 at threshold 0.8) is the direct no-fly competitor of any refusal score.
difference_from_tried: Tried: absolute response height instead of map-normalised score (z13_absolute_confidence_v1, inconclusive), utility heads on map/geometry (z13_next_utility_v1, z13_map_utility_v1), pairwise utility and peak ordering (z13_pairwise_utility_v1, z13_pairwise_map_v1), boundary-peak refusal (z13_boundary_readout_v1), score swap (z13_score_swap_v1), coverage tables at 1/2/5 % (e.g. 2 useful of 84 selected, z13_balanced_ridge_v1). Not tried: (i) a full risk-coverage/AURC comparison with oracle and random references and an explicit train26 -> dev35 separation-loss check across all scores (our coverage tables are points on this curve, not the curve with references); (ii) sequential accumulation of evidence across search frames with a pre-set false-refusal rate; (iii) separate heads for presence and position accuracy (partially overlapping with utility heads, which predict usefulness only). Point (i) is a measurement, not a new mechanism.
memory_write_policy: not applicable (no memory in the screened mechanisms, except confidence-gated updates discussed in other items).
distractor_representation: None in the screened sources (implicit at most).
refusal_evidence_horizon: (1)/(2): single sample. (3): sequential test over frames (e-process, alpha = 0.1). (6): learned accumulation over recent response maps (ConvLSTM). (7): current response vs its history. (4)/(5): per frame with temporal refinement over a window.
loss_on_applied_decision: (2): selection evaluated on the applied abstain decision at fixed coverage (risk-coverage); (5): accuracy-confidence head trained on the applied 'within 12 px' criterion; (3): no loss (statistical test). For us: the AURC protocol evaluates the applied decision (useful vs harmful correction), not the map.
association_entry_point: Track-state update gate: decide before matching whether the FlyVis correction replaces the Kalman center (refuse = keep Kalman prediction).
no_fly_control_equivalent: Kalman innovation / predicted-center uncertainty as a refusal score; shift-limit guard; matching-cost check; the same scoring on R1 input-eye maps.
hard_subset_evaluation: (1): separate evaluation per failure source (in-distribution, covariate shift, new class). (3): none (four generic benchmarks, 50 random videos each). Others not reported in screening.
temporal_information_availability: (1)/(2): per sample, no temporal issue. (3): causal, uses only past and current frames, but the alarm arrives with detection delay (average 25-178 frames in Table 3) - longer than our 30-frame loss episodes, so the benefit after accumulating evidence may arrive too late for the correction the tracker must apply now. (5): CoTracker3 online variant is causal over a sliding window; offline variant uses future frames.
depth_level: Short screening, as set in the item. Should not move to a full analysis as a mechanism; it should become a fixed measurement protocol (AURC with oracle/random references, train26 -> dev35) run on existing saved rows before any new refusal module, because it can show whether confidence on FlyVis maps separates useful from harmful corrections at all.
